nodes.prompt: A salesman offers a new tractor on EMI: ₹8,000/month for 5 years. Your current monthly income is ₹12,000. Should you buy it?

options.label: Rent a tractor this season (₹3,000 one-time)
Form a group with 3 neighbours and buy jointly

nodes.prompt: The EMI eats 67% of your income. One bad season and you default on the loan.
nodes.lesson: [Skill Tested: Budget Planning] EMI should never exceed 30-40% of your monthly income. A ₹8,000 EMI on a ₹12,000 income leaves no room for food, school fees, or emergencies.

nodes.prompt: Smart! Renting saved you from a debt trap. You paid just ₹3,000 and kept ₹9,000 free for other expenses.
nodes.lesson: [Skill Tested: Budget Planning] Renting equipment makes sense when you don't need it year-round. Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) offer government-subsidised machinery rentals.

nodes.prompt: Joint ownership works! Each farmer paid ₹40,000 and sharing the maintenance cost keeps everyone happy.
nodes.lesson: [Skill Tested: Budget Planning] Collective asset ownership is a cornerstone of rural financial resilience. Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) often provide equipment pools.
